summary: Backend tests for the self-service association creation feature. 21/21 pytest tests PASS covering: GET /api/public/associations/check-code/:code (available / taken / format-invalid), POST /api/public/associations/register (success creates source='self_service', all validation errors, duplicate code, JWT + code returned, admin persisted), GET /api/public/associations/:code/info (returns name/type/code, 404 for invalid/inactive, does NOT leak adminEmail/source/id), GET /api/platform/associations (every row includes the new 'source' field with values 'manual' or 'self_service'), POST /api/platform/associations (Super Admin path still 201 and produces source='manual', NOT affected by self-service limit), MAX_SELF_SERVICE_PER_USER=5 per-email limit correctly returns 403 on the 6th attempt, POST /api/auth/login (admin) and POST /api/platform/login (super-admin) regression both still 200.

minor.issue: Uses the same `registerLimiter` as POST /register (5 req/hour/IP, shared bucket). This means a legitimate user typing a code in the UI (real-time check on each keystroke) can quickly exhaust the register budget and be blocked from actually creating the association. Recommendation: give check-code its own lighter limiter (e.g. 60/hour) or reuse infoLimiter (30/hour) which is closer to its cost profile.

When only `adminPhone` is provided (no email), the code stores a synthetic email `admin_<timestamp>@temp.local`. Two rapid registrations in the same millisecond could theoretically collide on this synthetic address (User.email is unique). Very low probability, but consider using a UUID instead of Date.now() (routes/public.js line 174).

action_items: OPTIONAL / MINOR: Decouple the rate limiter on GET /check-code/:code from POST /register (currently both share registerLimiter 5/h/IP). This will affect real users who type codes character-by-character in the UI.

OPTIONAL / MINOR: Use crypto.randomUUID() or a random suffix instead of Date.now() when synthesising an email for phone-only admins (routes/public.js:174) to avoid rare collisions on the User.email unique index.
critical_code_review_comments: Positive: The register endpoint uses a Prisma $transaction() so the association and admin user are created atomically. Good.
Positive: MAX_SELF_SERVICE_PER_USER is env-configurable (parseInt(process.env.MAX_SELF_SERVICE_PER_USER || '5')) — good ops story.
Positive: /info endpoint whitelists returned fields (select: name/type/code/active) — no accidental leakage of adminEmail or source.
Positive: /platform/associations spreads the full record so the new 'source' field is exposed to the Platform console for the 'Libre-service' badge without extra code changes.
Positive: Code is normalized to uppercase before uniqueness check and DB insert (both in check-code and register), so a user typing 'my-club' and later 'MY-CLUB' will correctly hit the same row.
Design gap: registerLimiter is shared between check-code (idempotent read) and register (heavy write). A legitimate 8-character code entered live in the UI could burn 8 slots. Split limiters.

Design gap: The per-user cap (MAX_SELF_SERVICE_PER_USER) counts associations linked by ADMIN user email/phone, but a determined user can register with a fresh email each time. The code comment (lines 121-123) acknowledges this — acceptable guard-rail, not a real security control. Documented.
Minor: The synthetic email fallback for phone-only registration (`admin_${Date.now()}@temp.local`) is not truly unique under load — use randomUUID().

Minor: No length/character validation on `name` and `adminName` — a very long name (say 10 000 chars) will be accepted and stored. Consider a reasonable max (e.g., 200 chars) via Prisma or Pydantic-equivalent validation.
